question: Is the prefill-parity cap on the Apple GPU Vulkan driver a hardware issue limit or driver code generation? Establish the arithmetic ceiling precisely with a dependency-free FMA sweep, read the emitted AGX for best/worst arms, and attempt a real driver-side improvement on a fork branch.

base.work_branch: origin/hk/fma-ceiling-unroll @ c425187 (NEVER to be merged or installed; see verdict)

method.harness: hand-written Vulkan compute harness (harness/fma_bench.c) + GLSL/SPIR-V arm generator (harness/sweep.py); dependency-free FMA loops, independent accumulator chains, manual unroll, push-constant trip count, median of 9 reps after 3 warmups, ~0.19 ms dispatch overhead floor (cal arm) against 3.6-32 ms kernels
method.lock: every GPU run under one top-level flock /tmp/m1-gpu.lock on jwm1 (jwm1-linux, Apple M1 G13G B1)
method.asm: AGX_MESA_DEBUG=shaders dumps with MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE=true (cache masking found and worked around)

ceiling_results_gflop_s.units: GFLOP/s, median; 262144 invocations, 16384 FMA/thread, 2 flops per FMA

f32_best.name: f32_a8_u8_w128_p0
f32_best.note: 8 independent chains x 8 unroll; WG 32..512 flat; +40 extra live regs flat (no spill cliff)

f32_latency_bound.note: single serial chain is latency-bound; chains hide it

ceiling_results_gflop_s.f32_no_spill: p4..p40 extra live registers: 2147-2172 GFLOP/s (flat) -- no spills, occupancy not hurt

fp16_packed_best.note: f16vec2 hfma2 x2 -- 2x fp32 rate as expected

coopmat_muladd.note: hand-written SPIR-V (harness/coop_min*.spvasm), zero operand traffic, 8x8x8 f32 coopMatMulAdd under AGX_SIMDMAT=1

verdict_ceiling: The fp32 scalar FMA ceiling is 2303 GFLOP/s on this device (nominal 2617 GFLOP/s at 1024 lanes x 1.278 GHz; measured value implies ~1.13 GHz sustained). The hardware simd_matrix_fmadd32 path is NOT the limiter: with 4 independent accumulator chains it sustains 2148 GFLOP/s = 93% of the scalar ceiling. The 1440-1690 GFLOP/s ceilings measured by prior single-chain arms are chain-latency artifacts, not a silicon issue-rate limit and not a driver codegen cap.
codegen_findings: 1. Scalar FMA stream is clean: the best scalar arm's AGX loop is a tight fmadd sequence at the hardware ceiling -- no missed FMA formation, no spills, no scheduling loss to fix on the scalar path. [measured + dumps/f32_a8_u8_w128_p0.agx]

2. coopMatMulAdd loop body (dumps/coopmin_a8_u8_w128_p0.agx, final packed AGX): 'mov r8,r4; mov r9,r5; simd_matrix_fmadd32 r6,r8.abs.neg,r8,r6; iadd r3,r3,1; jmp_any' -- 2 loop-invariant aligned-pair MOVs + 3 control slots per ~16-cycle tile, and a single dependent chain exposes the fmadd's multi-cycle latency (~9 cycles/iter unaccounted = latency, matching the 1690 vs 2148+ ILP ladder). [measured]
3. agx_nir_lower_simdmat's muladd lowering does identity channel shuffles (subblk/nir_vec at nblk=1) and RA resolves loop-carried aligned-pair phis with per-iteration copies. [source read + dump]

4. nir_opt_loop_unroll REFUSES unknown-trip-count loops even with loop->control=nir_loop_control_unroll (check_unrolling_restrictions short-circuits, but simple/partial unroll both need a known or guessed trip count) -- so a marking pass cannot unroll app loops with runtime trip counts. [source read + measured no-op]

driver_patch_attempt.what: agx_nir_unroll_simdmat_loops(): marks enclosing loops of every simd_matrix_fmadd_agx intrinsic nir_loop_control_unroll, then runs nir_opt_loop_unroll; called from agx_preprocess_nir after nir_lower_vars_to_ssa. Files: agx_nir_lower_simdmat.c (+50), agx_nir.h (+1), agx_compile.c (+5).

measured.real_qmm_kernel_arm0_gate_up_1053x896x97: 1034 -> 817-820 GFLOP/s (-21%) on a release build of this exact commit, f16 digest 5179630cd4a7c3f9 IDENTICAL with and without the patch

driver_patch_attempt.verdict: REJECTED. Forces unroll of a const-trip loop in the shipped qmm kernel and loses more to occupancy/code size than it saves. Patch never installed as a package; installed driver untouched (hk6f6afc8-1 remains). Branch kept for the record, never to be merged.

real_kernel_ab.method: MLX_OMARCHY_QMM_COOP_BENCH probe (benchq/qmm-coop-bench/qmm_coop_bench_probe.py, venv-qmmcoop wheel 1aa2999b) run against the installed package vs a release meson build of the same commit 6f6afc8 with/without the patch (dev ICD, VK_DRIVER_FILES)
real_kernel_ab.digests: arm0 f16 digests 3e79733f76ed9d37 / 4e29e2dbdf33b57b / 5179630cd4a7c3f9 and arm4 digests reproduce the 2026-09-11-qmm-coop-datapath receipt exactly on both driver builds

implication_for_parity: Prefill headroom is KERNEL-side ILP, not driver codegen: the ceiling with 4 independent chains is 2148 GFLOP/s, and the shipped kernel (1032-1034) plus prior digest-preserving restructures (arms 1/2 regressed; arm 3 shared-load path 746) show the remaining gap is staging/loads and chain scheduling inside the MLX kernel, not fixable in the driver without the f16-operand lowering already named in the qmm-coop-datapath receipt.
